checks.democracy: NPR/GPB list of Jan. 6–7, 2021 objectors; PBS/AP; Senate Democrats floor record; AP Nov. 2020; Scripps Dec. 2020; Mediaite 2024 and 2026; Wikipedia. senate.gov roll-call pages could not be fetched. Re-checked 2026-10-08: NPR list via GPB lists him among the 6 senators sustaining the Arizona objection (93–6) and the 7 supporting the Pennsylvania objection. The Senate Democrats floor page confirms the 6–93 Arizona tally but does not list names. Official senate.gov roll-call pages were still unreachable, so the item stays 'news'. UPDATE 2026-10-14: certification votes confirmed from the Senate roll-call records themselves (votes 1 and 2 of the 117th Congress, 1st session, read by the records collector: Yea on both objections). Public statements on 2020 (Nov–Dec 2020, Nov 2024 Bannon interview) and 2026 already sourced, so democracy is 'done'.
checks.legal: CourtListener and efile/eFD domains were blocked by this environment's proxy, so federal dockets were not searched directly. Searched news archives (AP, APR, Alabama Reflector, ADN, Lagniappe, CNBC, Wikipedia) for civil/criminal cases, Senate Ethics matters and STOCK Act complaints. Found: the 2012–2013 TS Capital investor suit (settled), the 2021 STOCK Act late filings and CLC complaint to Senate Ethics (no public outcome found), and the 2026 residency quo warranto case (pending appeal). Alacourt is paywalled and was not searched. UPDATE 2026-10-14: the residency quo warranto appeal was decided Oct. 9, 2026 (Alabama Supreme Court affirmed dismissal for lack of jurisdiction; merits never reached). CourtListener/Justia still unreachable, so courts stays 'news'.

News and the 2020 Senate disclosure (secondary copy) show no foreign-government or foreign-business ties; the only foreign item found was trading in a China-based company's securities (Alibaba options, 2021).

democracy.t: After the 2020 election, likened results to referees adding touchdowns after a game ended — AP described this as backing Trump's unsupported fraud claim.
As senator-elect signaled he would join an objection to the Electoral College count ('You'll see what's coming'); Trump called him a 'hero'.
One of six senators who voted to sustain the objection to Arizona's electoral votes (failed 6–93).
One of seven senators who voted to sustain the objection to Pennsylvania's electoral votes (failed).
Voted against creating an independent commission on the Jan. 6 attack; told ABC News in 2025 he fully supported Trump's Jan. 6 pardons.
Told Steve Bannon that Democrats 'stole the election from President Trump' in 2020.
Said on Newsmax 'we probably have four or five senators that didn't legally win', offering no evidence or names.

eligibility_challenge.t: Two veterans (Brooke Lynn Dorgan and Justin Jude LeBlanc) filed a quo warranto suit claiming he does not meet the Alabama Constitution's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Montgomery Circuit Judge Brooke Reid dismissed it July 9, 2026 for lack of jurisdiction, without ruling on the facts. Plaintiffs appealed July 14. Tuberville, AG Steve Marshall and the Alabama GOP asked the court to affirm, and briefing closed Sept. 4, 2026. On Oct. 9, 2026 the Alabama Supreme Court affirmed the dismissal in an unsigned 13-page opinion, holding that a party nominee does not hold public office, so a quo warranto action cannot be brought against one, and that a primary-election contest is generally the only pre-election route to challenge a nominee's qualifications. The merits (where he lives) were never decided. Per the same report, a Covington County suit and two Alabama GOP complaints were also dismissed. Status as of 2026-10-14: closed at the state Supreme Court; plaintiffs' lawyer called the ruling disappointing. A separate primary challenge by Ken McFeeters was dismissed by the state GOP committee on June 14, 2026. To rebut that challenge, his lawyers filed seven years of redacted Alabama income-tax returns (June 1, 2026); the Alabama Department of Revenue declined a records request to confirm his state filing status.
